objective: Provide a project-scoped, independently maintained release calendar and fixed-category project announcements with member-authorized CRUD and responsive project presentation.
users: Project members viewing and maintaining their project's release arrangements.

requirements.statement: Add a project-detail release-calendar tab while preserving existing tab routes.
acceptance: Direct and interactive tab navigation load the calendar.

requirements.statement: Persist multiple independent entries containing title, release start date, release end date and remark; equal dates represent a single-day arrangement and ranges for one project cannot overlap.
acceptance: CRUD survives refresh
An entry spanning two months is returned by both intersecting month queries
The calendar marks every day in the inclusive range
A non-overlapping second entry is accepted
An overlapping range is rejected
counterexample: A range is saved but only its start date is displayed
Two active entries cover the same date
Reading or writing configuration-management release windows.

requirements.statement: Authorize project members on the server for calendar reads and writes.
acceptance: Non-members and cross-tenant callers are denied.

requirements.statement: Use a desktop month calendar and a mobile date-grouped list that expands an inclusive date range into each visible day.
acceptance: The specified mobile and desktop viewports have no page-level horizontal overflow
Cross-month ranges are visible in every intersecting month
counterexample: A desktop grid squeezed into the phone viewport
A range disappears from the month containing only its end date.

requirements.statement: Restyle project tabs after the configuration-management release-window navigation.
acceptance: Existing tabs remain usable and theme-readable.
counterexample: Replacing the navigation with unrelated styling.

requirements.statement: Project announcements use six fixed categories independent of project plan stages: project, requirement, development, test, production and data migration.
acceptance: Announcement management exposes exactly six category tabs
Each tab only lists its own category
Creating and pinning in one tab does not change another tab
counterexample: The form reads selectable project plan stages
A pinned announcement appears in every category

requirements.statement: The server validates announcement category codes while preserving project membership, tenant, entity, optimistic-lock and audit controls.
acceptance: Invalid category writes are rejected
Authorized CRUD remains project-scoped
Write actions remain audited
requirements.source: Existing project announcement contract plus user clarification

requirements.statement: The project overview aggregates announcements across the six categories and shows all pinned announcements plus the latest three non-pinned announcements, without plan-stage filtering.
acceptance: Pinned announcements are always shown
At most three non-pinned announcements are shown
Overview query does not depend on current plan dates
counterexample: Older non-pinned announcements crowd out newer ones
Overview hides announcements because no plan is active

requirements.statement: Existing announcement detail, edit, delete, loading, empty, failure and submitting states remain usable after category tabs are introduced.
acceptance: Detail dialog opens from overview and management lists
Retry and conflict feedback remain available
counterexample: Tab change applies a page-level blocking mask

invariants: Active date ranges for one project do not overlap.
Server-side tenant, membership, entity, optimistic-lock, and audit controls apply.
constraints: Vue 3 and existing Element Plus/UI patterns.
Project system module owns the API and data.

selected_approach.name: Project-detail independent calendar tab
selected_approach.reason: Retains project context while separating release scheduling from project plans and configuration-management windows.

components.name: ProjectView
components.responsibility: Tab routing, date-range form and responsive calendar interaction

components.name: ProjectService
components.responsibility: Project-scoped CRUD, range validation, membership authorization and audit

components.name: Flyway migration
components.responsibility: Backfill single dates into range columns and add the month-overlap index

interfaces.name: Project release calendar REST API
interfaces.contract: Month-overlap listing plus optimistic-lock CRUD with release_start_date <= release_end_date within a project scope.

data_flows.input: Project member selects project tab/month or submits an inclusive date range
transitions: Server validates project membership, tenant and start <= end
Service queries ranges intersecting the requested month
UI expands each returned range across visible days and renders calendar/mobile groups
data_flows.output: Authorized project-scoped entries visible on every date in each range.

error_handling.behavior: Deny on server and show no-permission state

security: Server-side membership, tenant and entity checks
performance: Load one month at a time
compatibility: Preserve existing project tabs and release-window behavior
Backfill existing single-date rows as same-day ranges
operations: Additive migration and retained records on rollback

verification_strategy.signal: Existing and new tabs navigate correctly
verification_strategy.method: Browser regression at desktop and mobile.

verification_strategy.signal: Persisted CRUD and denied unauthorized writes

assumptions.text: Project member relationship grants calendar maintenance authority.
assumptions.basis: User stated all project people can edit.
assumptions.falsifier: Owner requires an additional role or permission boundary.

decisions.decision: Use independently maintained project calendar data.
Store inclusive release_start_date and release_end_date; equal dates represent a single day and every date in the range is marked.
Backfill existing release_date rows to same-day ranges in an additive migration.
decisions.reason: Preserve existing calendar arrangements while changing the contract

decisions.decision: Use six fixed announcement category codes independent of project plan stages.
Overview shows all pinned announcements plus the latest three non-pinned announcements across all categories.

risks.impact: Entries disappear from one intersecting month or are marked on the wrong day
risks.mitigation: Range validation, overlap SQL tests, and desktop/mobile browser checks.
Preserve query-tab contract and browser regression.

approval.evidence: User confirmed the date-range design and fixed six-category announcement behavior with overview pin/latest filtering.
